question: What are the two main parts that make up the human body's structure?
explanation: Think of the body in two parts: the central core (axial) and the attached limbs (appendicular). You've got this! [learn more](GNS111_U1_T4#GNS111_U1_T4_h1)

question: Why do nurses use standard medical terms when writing in patient notes?

options.A: It replaces the need for writing detailed physical assessments
options.B: It speeds up the discharge process for surgical patients
options.C: It prevents dangerous misunderstandings among healthcare team members
options.D: It eliminates all charting errors in the emergency unit

explanation: When we all speak the same medical language, every nurse and doctor pictures the exact same thing, keeping our patients safe! [learn more](GNS111_U1_T4#GNS111_U1_T4_h1)

question: Which part of the body is known as the cervical region?
explanation: The cervical region is just the medical term for your neck, connecting your head down to your trunk. Easy peasy! [learn more](GNS111_U1_T4#GNS111_U1_T4_h2)

question: What parts of the body make up the axial region?
explanation: The axial region forms the main vertical center of your body: your head, neck, and trunk. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T4#GNS111_U1_T4_h2)

question: Which of these is considered part of the upper limb?
explanation: Your forearm is part of your upper limb, while thighs and feet are part of your lower limbs. Great job! [learn more](GNS111_U1_T4#GNS111_U1_T4_h3)

question: What is the main job of the lower limbs?
explanation: Our lower limbs are built to support our body weight and help us walk, run, and move around every day. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T4#GNS111_U1_T4_h3)

question: How many sections are made when using the nine-region mapping system for the abdomen?
explanation: Just like the name says, the nine-region method divides the tummy area into nine neat boxes using imaginary lines. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T4#GNS111_U1_T4_h4)

question: A patient with appendicitis will usually feel pain in which part of the abdomen?
explanation: The appendix hangs out in the right lower quadrant, which is why pain there often points straight to appendicitis! [learn more](GNS111_U1_T4#GNS111_U1_T4_h4)

question: Which of these body features can you find on the front (anterior) of the body?
explanation: The umbilicus (your belly button) is right there on the front of your trunk. Simple and clear! [learn more](GNS111_U1_T4#GNS111_U1_T4_h5)

question: Why do nurses use surface landmarks during a physical check-up?

options.A: They eliminate the need to palpate the abdomen
options.B: They replace diagnostic imaging like ultrasound
options.C: They help clinicians locate deeper internal structures safely
options.D: They measure exact body temperature variations

explanation: External markers act like a road map, helping us find hidden organs, blood vessels, and injection spots with confidence. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T4#GNS111_U1_T4_h5)

question: What is the biggest danger of writing poor or vague anatomical notes during a shift change?

options.A: Miscommunication leading to delayed or incorrect patient care
options.C: Immediate failure of hospital accreditation audits
options.D: Excessive paperwork for incoming shift nurses

explanation: Clear notes save lives! Vague descriptions make it hard for the next nurse to notice if a patient is getting worse. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T4#GNS111_U1_T4_h6)

question: If you are charting a wound right on the front of a patient's elbow, what medical term should you use?
explanation: The antecubital region is the medical name for the front of the elbow—also a favorite spot for drawing blood! [learn more](GNS111_U1_T4#GNS111_U1_T4_h6)
